content.text: Ames and Monsignor Lafelle conspire on a yacht in its smoking room to use Church law against Ketchim’s Colombian mine while manipulating immigration politics. Carmen rises through New York society but rejects its greed, charity spectacle, marriage schemes, and religious coercion. She gives her pearls to the impoverished Jude outside the Charity Ball. After Hawley-Crowles’s ruin and suicide, Carmen lives with the repentant Beaubien in a suburban cottage, joining Father Waite, Hitt, Haynerd, and others in studying God, mind, matter, evil, and Christ’s healing principle. At university she challenges racial prejudice and debates Doctor Morton in his laboratory. She helps transform the Express into a clean, reform-minded newspaper. At Ames’s mansion, she and Haynerd overhear his bribery of Congressman Wales; Carmen confronts Ames and escapes. Ames later visits Carmen in her Express office, where she explains their practical Christian mission.
